newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola falls to new lows on commercials, funds.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola falls to new lows on commercials, funds.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down at new contract lows in all months as trade fell to or near the C$10 a tonne limit on commercial and fund sales spurred by a USDA crop report.

"Commercials sold July, funds sold August and November. There were hundreds of unfilled commission sell orders in the July and August," a trader said. The USDA forecast U.S. soybean acreage at 70.85 million acres, more than expected by U.S. traders. July WCE futures crush margin rose to +0.03 Monday from -3.14 Friday. July-Nov spread at $24.50, July-Aug $7. Volume was 5,306 lots, or 106,120 tonnes, with 175 hedges.
July and August fell C$10 to the new lows of $373 and $365.80 while November fell $8.70 to $347.60 after it set a low of $346.50. Limits were expanded to C$15 a tonne for the next three sessions.
WCE will be closed Tuesday for Canada Day.

July flax fell $8.20 to $329.70, September fell $14.90 to a new low of $326.60 after hitting commission sell stops, November fell $12.70 after setting a new low of $291.10 on commercial selling. Sep-Nov spread at $5. Flax has two more sessions to trade at the expanded limits of C$15 a tonne.
Oats did not trade but were offered down by commercials.

July western barley lost $0.90 to $122.10 after it set a new low of $122, PCTS sold October down $0.70 to $126.60 after it set a new low of $126.50 on commercial sales. Seventy July-Oct $4. Volume was 600 lots.
PCTS and locals bought December feed wheat down $0.40 to $153.30 from LFG after it set a low of $153, October fell $0.30 to $153.30 after it set a low of $153.10. Volume 400.
Commercials sold 20 October feed pea contracts down US$3.50 to US$174.50 after it set a new low of US$174 and 40 December down US$1.80 to US$172.50 after it set a new low of US$172.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, peas.)
